text: In this town, there is a big red button at the top of the clock tower.
Nobody knows what it does. There is a sign. It says: do not press.
Grandpa says it was here before the town. The mayor says it's for emergencies.
My little brother Pip says it's for him.
Today was the town fair. Balloons, music, a pie contest, and the mayor's very important speech.
While everyone was listening, Pip disappeared.
Then I saw him. At the top of the clock tower. Right next to the button.
I yelled, Pip, no! He pressed it.
The mayor's dog started talking. In a very deep voice. It said: good afternoon.
Pip pressed it again. All the cows started to float.
Again. The mayor shrank to the size of a mouse. His speech got very squeaky.
Again. The mailman turned into a chicken. He still delivered the mail.
Again. It started raining spaghetti.
I ran up the stairs. Two hundred stairs. Pip pressed it nine more times.
Grandma's hair turned into fireworks. The fountain sprayed lemonade. The houses started dancing.
When I reached the top, I grabbed Pip's hand. Just in time.
But Pip looked at me, smiled, and said: one more.
He pressed it with his other hand.
There was a flash. And when I opened my eyes...
I was Pip. And there was another Pip, right next to me.
